description:
Which models to run evals and readings against. Never one model alone.

The point of more than one is not redundancy, it is bias. Every model has a house style — one terse and prone to missing things, another expansive and prone to inventing them. A skill measured against a single model is measured against that model's habits as much as its own merit, and a reading produced by one model is a single opinion wearing the clothes of a conclusion. Where two disagree, that disagreement is the finding.

Availability is discovered at run time: an entry here is an intention, not a promise the machine can reach it. Entries are ordered by reliability first, because a roster entry that reliably fails is worse than one that is merely a version behind.
_no_gemini_note: Gemini is deliberately not a default anywhere in this file. The API errors out or times out the overwhelming majority of the time from this account, and a default that usually fails is worse than one that is merely imperfect. The entries remain, demoted, so they can be promoted if that changes.
_arms_note: Models that play the reviewer under test. These run INSIDE pioneer's sandbox, which is narrower than the host: a sandboxed pi sees only part of the host's model registry. As of pioneer 0.3.5, openai-codex and google resolve; claude-code and jetbrains still fail with 'model not found' (a registry propagation gap, worth reporting upstream with that exact wording) and kimi-coding fails asking for /login. Until claude-code resolves, every arm entry below is one provider, so the diversity here is generational rather than cross-family — a real limitation, recorded rather than disguised.

arms.note: Verified inside the sandbox on pioneer 0.3.5.

A third codex line, verified in the sandbox. Use when one of the two above is unavailable.
Resolves in the sandbox, and would be genuine cross-family diversity — but see _no_gemini_note. Demoted, not removed.

_readers_note: Models that read transcripts in the third pass. These run OUTSIDE the sandbox, so the full host registry is available and genuine cross-family diversity is possible here even while the arms are constrained to one provider. Two are used per pass; where they disagree, that is reported rather than resolved.
